```{python}
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
import _dpm as dpm

con = dpm.connect(db or None)
history = dpm.versions(con, table_code)
if not history:
    raise SystemExit(f"{table_code} is not a template in this database.")
current = history[-1]
cells = dpm.cells(con, current["table_vid"])
dimensions = dpm.dimensions(con, current["table_vid"])
checks = dpm.rules(con, table_code)
drift = dpm.moved(con, current["table_vid"])
wording = dpm.relabelled(con, current["table_vid"])
first, last = history[0]["from_release"], dpm.releases(con)[-1]["code"]
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(
    f"{len(cells):,} reportable cells, {len(dimensions)} dimensions, "
    f"{len(checks):,} validation rules reaching it, "
    f"{sum(1 for check in checks if not check['active']):,} of them switched off. "
    f"Current version in force since DPM {current['from_release']}; "
    f"the template has existed since {first}, and this database goes to {last}.\n"
)
```

## What a description is made of

There is nothing to copy. `VariableVersion.Name` is NULL for every row in the DPM, so a
datapoint has no sentence of its own: every description, here and in the supervisory
portals, is composed from the template, the row and the column. That is why two tools can
agree on the wording without either of them owning it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
for cell in cells[:3]:
    print(f"- `{cell['cell_code']}` — {dpm.described(cell, current['name'])}")
print()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
published = dpm.official()
here = [(cell, published[(table_code, cell["row_code"])]) for cell in cells
        if (table_code, cell["row_code"]) in published]
if here:
    rows_covered = len({cell["row_code"] for cell, _ in here})
    celex = here[0][1].get("celex", "")
    link = f"https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:{celex}" if celex else ""
    print(
        f"\n### The same rows in Swedish and German\n\n"
        f"Not a translation: the templates are an annex to an Implementing Regulation, and "
        f"an Implementing Regulation is published in all 24 official languages. "
        f"{rows_covered} of this template's rows have a published wording.\n"
    )
    if celex:
        # Which text, not just that there is one. The act is amended, and a row's wording
        # is a wording of one consolidated version of it.
        print(
            f"\nFrom [{celex}]({link}), the consolidated regulation as it applies from "
            f"{celex[-8:-4]}-{celex[-4:-2]}-{celex[-2:]}. Earlier consolidations word some "
            "rows differently, so this is the wording of one version and not of the act "
            "for all time.\n"
        )
    seen, listing = set(), []
    for cell, found in here:
        if cell["row_code"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(cell["row_code"])
        listing.append({
            "row": cell["row_code"],
            "English": cell["row_label"][:48],
            "Svenska": found["sv"][:48],
            "Deutsch": found["de"][:48],
            # `stem` means the Journal printed this grid once, under the template this
            # one is a variant of. Said, rather than quietly presented as its own.
            "from": found.get("from", "journal"),
        })
    print(dpm.markdown_table(listing[:12], ["row", "English", "Svenska", "Deutsch", "from"]))
    if len(listing) > 12:
        print(f"\n_{len(listing) - 12} more; source/its_labels.csv has them all._")
    print()

    # Only where the regulation itself reworded a row. 16 templates of 165 have any, so
    # on most pages this prints nothing, which is the point: a page that says nothing
    # about versions is a page where the version does not change the answer.
    earlier = dpm.reworded()
    touched = [(cell, earlier[(table_code, cell["row_code"])]) for cell, _ in here
               if (table_code, cell["row_code"]) in earlier]
    said = set()
    for cell, trail in touched:
        if cell["row_code"] in said or len(trail) < 2:
            continue
        said.add(cell["row_code"])
        if len(said) == 1:
            print("\n#### Rows the regulation has reworded\n")
            print("The datapoint did not change and neither did the cell. The sentence did.\n")
        print(f"\n**{cell['row_code']}**\n")
        for step in trail:
            print(f"- `{step['celex']}` — {step['en'][:84]}")
        print()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
defined = dpm.instructions()
spelled = [(cell, defined[(table_code, cell["row_code"])]) for cell in cells
           if (table_code, cell["row_code"]) in defined]
if spelled:
    seen, shown = set(), 0
    where = spelled[0][1].get("celex", "")
    print(
        "\n### What the regulation says these rows are\n\n"
        "From the instructions annex, which gives each row its meaning and the article "
        "that requires it. Also published in every official language"
        + (f", here from {where}" if where else "")
        + ".\n"
    )
    for cell, found in spelled:
        if cell["row_code"] in seen or shown >= 4:
            continue
        seen.add(cell["row_code"])
        shown += 1
        print(f"\n**{cell['row_code']} — {cell['row_label'][:70]}**\n")
        print(f"> {found['en'][:420]}\n")
        print(f"> _{found['sv'][:420]}_\n")
    rows_defined = len({cell['row_code'] for cell, _ in spelled})
    if rows_defined > shown:
        print(f"\n_{rows_defined - shown} more rows are spelled out; source/its_instructions.csv has them._\n")
```

## What it breaks down by

The members are given in the model's own wording, which is the wording a query has to
match. A near miss matches nothing rather than erroring, and a trailing space is a real
difference in this model.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dpm.markdown_table(
    [{**row, "wording": row["wording"][:160]} for row in dimensions],
    ["dimension", "members", "wording"],
))
print()
```

## What has changed

The EBA ships no account of this: the `ChangeLog` table is present and empty in every
release. What follows is read off the version rows — `StartReleaseID` and `EndReleaseID`
on the table, the variable and the header — rather than from a changelog.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dpm.markdown_table(history, ["from_release", "to_release", "table_vid", "name"]))
print()
print(
    f"\nOf the {drift['variables']:,} datapoints this version reports, "
    f"**{drift['moved']:,} have sat at another row or column** at some point since "
    f"{first}. The datapoint is the thing that persisted; the coordinate is where it "
    "happened to be that release — which is why a time series keyed on the coordinate "
    "is keyed on an address.\n"
)
print(
    f"\nA further {drift['shared']:,} are reported by more than one template. That is "
    "the layout, not a change: the variants of a template share datapoints.\n"
)
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
if wording:
    print("### Rows and columns whose wording changed\n")
    print("The coordinate stayed, the datapoint stayed, the sentence shown to a reader did not.\n")
    print(dpm.markdown_table(
        [{**row, "label": row["label"][:90]} for row in wording],
        ["code", "from_release", "to_release", "label"],
    ))
else:
    print("No row or column of this template has been reworded since it was introduced.")
print()
```

## What checks it

`active` is the EBA's deactivated-rules list. A description that tells a reader to
satisfy a rule nobody runs is worse than one that names no rule at all.

Each code links to what it checks, under this release. A code is not a stable statement:
2 005 of 7 514 consecutive versions of a rule change the expression, and others change
only the severity — `v0174_m` is an error up to DPM 4.1 and a warning from 4.2. So "the
file passed v0174_m" means nothing without the release it was checked under.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dpm.markdown_table(
    [check | {"rule_code": dpm.rule_link(check["rule_code"], last)} for check in checks[:25]],
    ["rule_code", "severity", "active", "rows_here"],
))
if len(checks) > 25:
    print(f"\n_{len(checks) - 25:,} more; the whole list is a query, not a page._")
print()
```
